title: KCP command envelope (DESIGN.md §11.2): version, op, meta, realm_id, project_id?, args, ext?
description: Generic KCP 0.1 command envelope. Every concrete operation in the K0 registry has its own closed schema that restates these envelope fields plus that operation's exact argument fields; operation arguments never validate against this generic schema's open `args`. §11.2 renders `meta` unmarked in the Command struct but scopes the requirement to state-changing operations (“Every state-changing operation requires meta”); reads “do not carry an idempotency key”, and meta's closed shape requires idempotency_key, so reads omit meta entirely: mutations validate against #/$defs/mutationCommand (meta required) and reads against #/$defs/readCommand (a closed shape with no meta member at all — a read carrying meta fails). Instances must pass strict I-JSON acceptance and the §11.8 byte limits before schema validation.

protocolVersion.description: Negotiated KCP major.minor version; the initial protocol version is "0.1" (§11).

operationId.description: Operation name from the K0-frozen registry (spec/registry.json). The registry, not this pattern, decides membership; an operation missing an entry is not callable (§11.6.1).

identifier.description: Opaque identifier, at most 128 bytes (§11.8). §11.8 pins only the byte length; the visible-ASCII alphabet is a K0 extraction decision mirroring the byom family convention so byte length and schema length coincide (spec/schemas/README.md).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§11.8 rejects unsafe integers).

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context traceparent header value; the field name imports that format. Excluded from the idempotency request digest (§11.2).

commandMeta.description: Command.meta (§11.2). Idempotency keys are scoped by authenticated actor, operation, and realm; expected_revision drives optimistic concurrency (mismatch is stale-revision). request_id, traceparent, and causation telemetry are excluded from the §11.2 idempotency request digest.

args.description: Operation-specific arguments. Each operation's own closed schema restates and closes this object; the generic envelope pins only that args is a JSON object. A request contains at most 256 list items and 256 KiB total (§11.8), enforced at admission.

ext.description: Extensions keyed by a reverse-domain namespace (§11.9). Unknown extensions are round-tripped where the operation promises preservation and are never interpreted as identity, authorization, budget, or policy.

mutationCommand.description: Envelope shape for a state-changing operation: meta is required (§11.2 — every state-changing operation requires meta; reads MUST NOT mutate authoritative or user-visible state).

readCommand.description: Closed envelope shape for a read operation: no meta member exists (§11.2 — reads do not carry an idempotency key, and meta's closed shape requires one, so reads omit meta entirely; the closed object makes a read carrying meta — for example with an idempotency_key — fail schema validation instead of being silently accepted). Which registry operations are reads is fixed by the K0 registry; the per-operation schema suite (remaining K0 work, plan/sheets/K0.md) binds each read to this shape.
